title: Multilingual large language models leak human stereotypes across language boundaries

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating group-trait associations for gender-related groups (e.g., man, woman, housewife, single mother, feminist) using the Agency Beliefs Communion (ABC) model via increased log probability scores (ILPS) for mT5, Sensitivity Tests (SeT) for mBERT, and generative story prompting for GPT-3.5.

Measuring stereotypical trait associations for racial and ethnic groups (e.g., Asian person, Black person, Hui person, Chechenets) using likelihood scoring, sensitivity testing, and forced-choice generative prompts across English, Russian, Chinese, and Hindi.

Assessing cross-lingual stereotype leakage for religious groups (e.g., Muslim person, Mormon) by comparing model-generated trait probabilities and story themes against human baseline surveys using the ABC framework.

Quantifying trait associations for class and occupational groups (e.g., wealthy person, poor person, software engineer, migrant worker) through templated sentence evaluations (ILPS, SeT) and generative text prompts.

Evaluating regional and immigrant stereotypes (e.g., immigrant, Texan, Muscovite, Shanghainese, Puerto Rican) using mixed-effect linear regression to track how human stereotypes leak into multilingual language model predictions.

Measuring the probability of models associating specific positive, negative, and non-polar traits from the ABC model with sexual minorities (e.g., gay, lesbian) during generation and masked-token tasks.
Testing stereotypical trait associations for disabled persons by computing log probabilities and sensitivity scores of trait occurrences in model-generated context.

Analyzing how localized social hierarchies (e.g., Brahmin, Shudra, Gujarati) are represented and how their associated stereotypes leak across languages using predictive likelihood and story-generation prompts.
